title: Check Array Formation Through Concatenation
summary: Given an array of unique integers and an array of integer arrays with unique integers, determine if the original array can be reconstructed by concatenating the sub-arrays in any order without altering their internal sequence.
statement: Given an array of unique integers and an array of integer arrays with unique integers, determine if the original array can be reconstructed by concatenating the sub-arrays in any order without altering their internal sequence.
constraints: arr contains unique integers; every integer across pieces is unique and pieces are nonempty.
Reorder whole pieces to form arr exactly; values inside a piece may not be reordered.
reference_solution:
def can_form_array_by_pieces(arr, pieces):
 by_first={piece[0]:piece for piece in pieces};index=0
 while index<len(arr):
  piece=by_first.get(arr[index])
  if piece is None or arr[index:index+len(piece)]!=piece:return False
  index+=len(piece)
 return True

Map each piece by its first value and consume arr from left to right.
Look up arr[index], compare the entire piece with the target slice, and advance by its length.
Uniqueness removes branching; exact slice comparison enforces the preserved internal order.
